memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: He led you through the vast and dreadful wilderness, that thirsty and waterless land, with its venomous snakes and scorpions. He brought you water out of hard rock. He gave you manna to eat in the wilderness, something your ancestors had never known, to humble and test you so that in the end it might go well with you. You may say to yourself, "My power and the strength of my hands have produced this wealth for me." But remember the Lord your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth, and so confirms his covenant, which he swore to your ancestors, as it is today. - Deut 8:15-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses exposes the proud thought that creeps into a comfortable heart: "My power and the strength of my hands have produced this wealth for me." It is the whisper of self-sufficiency — the belief that we made ourselves, that our success is entirely our own doing. God's answer is a call to remember the truth: "it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth." Even our strength, our skills, our opportunities are gifts from His hand.

This is a humbling and freeing truth. Everything we have and everything we are able to do flows ultimately from God. The health to work, the mind to think, the very breath in our lungs — all are His gifts. We did not create ourselves or our abilities. When we forget this, we grow proud and take credit that belongs to God. When we remember it, we grow grateful and humble, recognising ourselves as stewards of gifts we were freely given.

The apostle Paul asked the piercing question, "What do you have that you did not receive?" (1 Cor 4:7). If everything is a gift, there is no room for boasting. This does not diminish hard work or diligence — God calls us to those. But it means we work with open hands and grateful hearts, knowing the One who gives the strength. Whatever you have achieved, remember who gave you the ability. Let your successes lead you to worship, not pride, and hold your accomplishments as gifts to steward for His glory.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I take credit for my success, or recognise God as the giver of my abilities?
- How does remembering "God gives the ability" keep me humble?
- What do I have that I did not ultimately receive from God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, everything I have and every ability I possess comes from You. Guard me from the pride that says "I did this myself." Help me to work with grateful, open hands, remembering that You give me the strength, and to use all I have for Your glory. Amen.
